definitions.gloss: May blues; a state of lethargy or depression affecting new employees and students in May
definitions.explanation: a form of adjustment disorder common in Japan, occurring around May when the initial excitement of a new job or school year wears off and reality sets in after the Golden Week holiday

examples.japanese: ⟦{新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}→新入社員：15536_shinnyuushain⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{五月病|ごがつびょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧やすい。
examples.english: New employees are prone to May blues.

examples.japanese: ⟦ゴールデンウィーク→ゴールデンウィーク：22760_goorudenwiiku⟧⟦{明|あ}け→明け：13157_ake⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{五月病|ごがつびょう}になった。
examples.english: I got the May blues after Golden Week ended.

examples.japanese: {五月病|ごがつびょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧せず⟦{休養|きゅうよう}→休養：11450_kyuuyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大事|だいじ}→大事：01253_daiji⟧だ。
examples.english: To prevent May blues, it's important to rest and not push yourself too hard.

notes:
FORMS:
⟦{五月|ごがつ}→五月：00625_gogatsu⟧ (May) + {病|びょう} (illness) → May sickness

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the fiscal and academic year begins in April. By May, after the long Golden Week holiday (⟦ゴールデンウィーク→ゴールデンウィーク：22760_goorudenwiiku⟧), new employees and students often experience:
- Loss of motivation
- Fatigue and exhaustion
- Difficulty adjusting to new environment
- Feelings of inadequacy

SYMPTOMS:
- ⟦やる{気|き}→やる気：05089_yaruki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}ない→出る：00513_deru⟧ (lack of motivation)
- ⟦{疲|つか}れ→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧やすい (easily tired)
- ⟦{食欲|しょくよく}→食欲：03249_shokuyoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (loss of appetite)
- ⟦{眠|ねむ}れない→眠れる：15166_nemureru⟧ (insomnia)
